flags.title: SNAP ABAWD Work Requirements — March 1, 2026
flags.summary: Starting March 1, 2026, ABAWD work requirements apply statewide in Illinois — prior waiver ended. ABAWDs ages 18–54 must document 80 hours/month of work, education, or qualifying activity.

flags.title: Illinois Medicaid — Expanded, All Adults to 138% FPL
flags.summary: Illinois expanded Medicaid under the ACA. Adults 19–64 earning up to 138% FPL qualify for Medicaid. There is NO coverage gap for childless adults. Undocumented adults 42+ qualify for Immigrant Health Connect (state-funded).

flags.title: Chicago Minimum Wage $16.20/hr — HIGHER than State $15.00/hr
flags.summary: Chicago minimum wage is $16.20/hr as of July 2024 — higher than Illinois state minimum of $15.00/hr. Always check Chicago wage before calculating back wages for any Chicago worker.

flags.title: Chicago Just Cause Eviction Ordinance — Stronger Than State Law
flags.summary: Chicago enacted the Residential Landlord and Tenant Ordinance (RLTO) with strong tenant protections, including 30-day written notice for lease non-renewal and a 14-day cure period for non-payment.

flags.title: Illinois TANF (TANF Cash Assistance) — $432/mo Max, 60-Month Limit
flags.summary: Illinois TANF pays up to $432/month for a family of 3 with a 60-month lifetime limit. Work requirements apply at 30 hours/week.

flags.title: IDHR Election-of-Remedies — File Carefully
flags.summary: Filing with the Illinois Department of Human Rights (IDHR) may bar you from filing in state court on the same claim. Always consult legal aid before filing.

flags.title: Illinois Workers' Compensation — Mandatory for Most Employers
flags.summary: Illinois requires virtually all employers to carry workers' compensation insurance. Route all workplace injury cases to the Illinois Workers' Compensation Commission.

flags.title: Chicago Cooling Centers & Utility Shutoff — Summer Heat Critical
flags.summary: Utilities cannot shut off during heat emergencies (90°F+). Chicago activates cooling centers when heat index reaches 95°F. Enroll in ComEd/Nicor medical baseline rate program if chronic illness.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Illinois Emergency Admission
flags.message: IL involuntary psychiatric hold law: Illinois Emergency Admission. Statutory authority: 405 ILCS 5/3-600. Maximum initial hold duration: 24 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 24 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in IL retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in IL: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Illinois Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Illinois Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
